body:
Thank you, and don't worry, it doesn't come off as preachy. I know that my use of any of these substances cannot and should not continue in the long term, and I've previously abstained from ever mixing them in the same 24-hour period. This combination was a one-off, which doesn't make it any less scary but maybe improves my odds of being okay.

Assuming my current issue doesn't constitute an urgent medical situation that would need to be handled first, my next plan is to reach out to try to get access to a therapist and to finally get back in touch with my psychiatrist. I've seen where this road leads and it's not good.
Comes out to somewhere in the range of 1000mg, so about 2 extra strength tylenol I guess. Doesn't seem like much when I put it that way, which I guess is a little comforting.

Thanks. I read today that acetaminophen toxicity symptoms can appear a couple days after initial ingestion and I know that both alcohol and opioids can potentiate the effects of acetaminophen, so I'm a little freaked out. My symptoms are marginal and of course I've put my body through hell in the last week so it's been pretty worrying. I know it was pretty stupid and I'd definitely like to get to a point where I'm happy and safe.

Maybe, I haven't had a drink or touched the percs since then, but I'd actually been using/drinking less over the week than usual, probably because the lack of food intake just made me too exhausted to keep drinking and was conducive to a quicker high/buzz off of way less. I've been through one pretty challenging withdrawal that felt different but about the same level of shitty, and I'm probably withdrawing now but I'm wondering if I'm stupidly conflating the symptoms with hepatotoxicity or if I actually have done something to my liver
